sentences.text:
Opposite Parties
 Mr. P. Satpathy, Addl. Pp
 Mr. J.K. Panda, Advocate (informant)
 Coram:

Justice G. Satapathy
 Order(Oral)
01.12.2025 Order No.
05. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.

This is a bail application U/S.483 of BNSS by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Morada P.S. Case No. 123 of 2022 corresponding to C.T. Case No. 61 of 2022, pending in the file of learned P.O., Special Court under POCSO Act, Mayurbhanj, Baripada, for commission of offences punishable U/s.376-AB of IPC r/w. Sec. 6 of the POCSO Act and Sec. 3(2)(v) of S.C. & S.T. (PoA)
Act, on the main allegation of committing rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon the victim aged about less than 10 years by taking advantage of her caste belonging to SC.

3. Heard, Mr. Suryakanta Dwibedi, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. P. Satpathy, learned Addl.
Public Prosecutor and Mr. Jugal Kishore Panda, learned counsel for the informant/victim in the matter and perused the record.
4. Admittedly, the petitioner is in custody since 24.04.2023, but the trial is yet to be concluded and only 12 out of 23 charge sheeted witnesses have been examined.
However, the petitioner is aged about 76 years and is suffering from Parkinson disease as well as cataract problem as per the report submitted by the Jail Superintendent.

In such view of the matter, especially when the petitioner being an old person is facing the trial and the trial being not concluded even after more than two years custody of the petitioner, this Court without expressing any view on merits, admits the petitioner to bail.

entities.text: Nunugu @ Suresh Mohakud vs State Of Odisha & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, the bail application of the Petitioner stands allowed and the Petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty-five Thousand) only with one solvent surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the petitioner shall not contact the victim or visit her house or place of residence till disposal of the case,
(ii) the petitioner shall not threaten the informant or shall not coerce, induce or influence any of the witnesses acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts before the learned trial Court.
6.
Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
